title_en: Official Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Handling Escaped or Recidivist Offenders Undergoing Reform through Labor and Persons Undergoing Reeducation through Labor

articles.content_en: I. Regarding the question of whether the "Decision" may apply to impose severe or heavier punishment on a criminal who commits another crime during the period of reform through labor. Paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the "Decision" only provides that a reform-through-labor offender who commits another crime after escaping constitutes a statutory circumstance for severe or heavier punishment. Therefore, the "Decision" shall not apply to a criminal who commits another crime during the period of reform through labor but does not commit a crime after escaping during that period. However, the commission of another crime during the period of reform through labor shall be considered as a discretionary circumstance for severe punishment and shall be taken into account when imposing the sentence.

II. Regarding the question of whether the "Decision" may apply to impose severe punishment on a person who, after completing the term of reform through labor and remaining at the venue for employment, commits another crime. Paragraph 2 of Article 2 of the "Decision" provides that a person who commits another crime after being released upon completion of the sentence shall be subject to severe punishment. A person who, after completing the term of reform through labor and remaining at the venue for employment, commits another crime falls within the scope of "committing another crime after being released upon completion of the sentence." Therefore, the "Decision" shall apply to such criminal conduct, and severe punishment shall be imposed.

III. Regarding the question of whether a person subject to re-education through labor who commits a crime during the period of re-education through labor may be subject to severe or heavier punishment. We agree with the opinion of your court: for a person subject to re-education through labor who commits a crime during the period of re-education through labor, unless the circumstances fall within the provisions of Article 3 of the "Decision" and shall be subject to severe or heavier punishment, the "Decision" shall not apply to other criminal acts committed during the period of re-education through labor. However, such acts may be considered as discretionary circumstances for severe punishment and shall be taken into account when imposing the sentence.
June 11, 1990
